FICTIONAL REPLY NOTE — GENERAL REVIEW CONTROL

The working note repeats Brown v. Board of Education, 347 U.S. 483 (1954), as a research lead. It also writes Miranda v. Arizona, 347 U.S. 483 (1954), an intentional conflict between a caption and reporter citation. Keep the written caption separate from whichever decision a database returns.

The proposed remedy again mentions 42 U.S.C. § 1983. The note has no independent verification of statutory applicability or historical version.

The team wants a general map of the involved references before deciding how to prepare a reply. A complete occurrence-by-occurrence audit of every attachment is not requested here.
